artworks.title: Priam Asking Achilles for the Body of Hector
artworks.description: Oil painting by the young Alexander Ivanov, now in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow. The aged king of Troy kneels before Achilles and clasps the hands that slew his son, begging that Hector's body be released for burial — the supplication that closes the Iliad, where Priam kisses 'the terrible, man-slaying hands that had slain his many sons.'

artworks.title: Priam Pleading with Achilles for the Body of Hector
artworks.description: Canvas by the Scottish neoclassical painter Gavin Hamilton, who worked in Rome and devoted a celebrated cycle of history paintings to subjects from the Iliad; this one is now in the Tate collection, London. The old king has crossed the Greek camp by night to the tent of Achilles, to plead for the corpse of the son who was Troy's last defence.

artworks.title: Priam at the Feet of Achilles
artworks.description: The painting with which Jérôme-Martin Langlois, a pupil of David, won the Prix de Rome in 1809; it is kept at the École nationale supérieure des Beaux-Arts in Paris. In the torch-lit tent, Priam in his heavy red mantle kneels at the couch of the young Achilles and presses the hero's hand to his face, while attendants look on in silence.

films.title: Troy
films.description: Peter O'Toole's Priam walks into Achilles' tent to beg for Hector's body — the Iliad's last mercy, played as the film's quietest and hardest scene.

films.title: Helen of Troy
films.description: Wise's epic keeps Priam on the walls as Troy's last king — the father who watches sons fall and still opens the gate for Helen.

films.title: Troy: Fall of a City
films.description: The BBC/Netflix cycle gives Priam the long siege: a king holding a doomed city while his house tears itself between Paris and Hector.

films.title: Helen of Troy
films.description: John Rhys-Davies' Priam orders the infant Paris abandoned, then welcomes him home — the king whose mercy and stubbornness both doom Troy.

films.title: The Trojan Horse
films.description: Carlo Tamberlani plays Priam in Ferroni's peplum — the aged king of Troy as Aeneas fights through the city's last year.

music.title: Les Troyens
music.description: Berlioz opens his Virgilian epic in Priam's Troy — the king, the horse, and the night the city falls before Aeneas' flight begins.

music.title: King Priam
music.description: Tippett's own libretto makes Priam the tragic centre — the father who orders Paris killed to save the city, then lives every consequence.

music.title: Paris
music.description: English and Mackay's musical keeps Priam as Troy's father-king — the palace that must absorb Paris' choice and the war that follows.

popCulture.title: Hamlet
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: The Player's speech on Priam's slaughter still haunts Hamlet — 'What's Hecuba to him' hangs on the image of the old king cut down.

popCulture.title: A Thousand Ships
popCulture.creator: Natalie Haynes
popCulture.description: Haynes' women's Trojan War keeps Hecabe and the royal house in view — Priam as the father whose city and sons are taken one by one.

popCulture.title: Troy (novel series)
popCulture.creator: David Gemmell
popCulture.description: Gemmell's trilogy restages the siege with Priam's court at the centre — the king of Troy in bestselling heroic fantasy.

popCulture.title: Troilus and Cressida
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: Shakespeare's bitter Troy keeps Priam among the Trojan elders — the aged king watching a war that will not end cleanly.
